title: Alert tuning for overload protection: reduce noise/flapping post-canary
creator: Rafael Mendes
content:
Context
- After canary enablement (us-east, limited model set) we’re seeing alert noise from breaker transitions and load-shedding signals that are expected during controlled overload, plus some genuine flapping during recovery.
- Goal: reduce paging/noise without masking real regressions (queue runaway, control plane unresponsiveness, elevated internal 5xx).

Why this ticket exists
- Current alert set (from overload dashboard + initial rules in observability-pack/pr-611) was intentionally sensitive for early rollout.
- Now that we have canary data, tune:
  1) breaker hysteresis-related alerting (don’t page on expected open/half-open transitions)
  2) alert windows (avoid 1–2m transient blips)
  3) signal quality (use ratios and burn-rate style alerts where possible)

Inputs / evidence to use
- Canary period: 2026-01-20 through 2026-02-03 (us-east, 2 models, hosted traffic + synthetic overload from perf-canary)
- Dashboards: Overload Protection dashboard (Grafana) panels: breaker state by (model, tier), shed rate by reason, queue depth, p95/p99 latency, internal 5xx.
- Incident thread notes: a few near-pages where breaker state oscillated during recovery and created repetitive notifications.
- SLO accounting changes: slo-toolkit/pr-204 separates “overload-protected” errors from internal failures; alerts must align to that.

Observed problems (canary)
1) Breaker transition alert flapping
- Symptom: breaker_open transitions for (model=X, tier=free) oscillate open/half-open for ~8–12 minutes after spike, generating repeated WARN + PAGE.
- Root cause hypotheses:
  - recovery probes too aggressive (half-open allows too much traffic too quickly)
  - alert evaluated on raw transition count rather than sustained open state

2) Shed-rate alert too sensitive during controlled overload tests
- Symptom: paging on shed_rate > 1% for 3 minutes even when overload is intentional and system stays healthy (latency stable, control plane ok).
- We need to page only when shed is (a) unexpected (no corresponding high-load signal), or (b) persistent enough to risk customer impact / error budget.

3) Queue depth/latency alerts fire before customer-impact thresholds
- Symptom: queue depth spikes on a single shard triggers page, but latency and internal failure rate remain within SLO.
- We should use multi-signal correlation (queue depth + p99 latency + internal error rate) or longer windows.

Proposed changes (initial)
A) Breaker state alerts
- Replace “transition count” paging with “sustained open” paging:
  - PAGE if breaker_state == OPEN for >= 15m AND request_volume > N (to avoid low-traffic false positives)
  - WARN if breaker_state == OPEN for >= 5m
- Add “flapping detector” as WARN only:
  - flapping = transitions(open<->half-open/closed) >= 6 within 10m
  - route to #eng-sre + dashboard annotation; do not page unless paired with elevated internal failures

B) Shed rate / overload protected error alerts
- Use SLO toolkit separation:
  - Do not page solely on overload-protected error ratio (429/503 w/ overload code).
  - Page if internal 5xx ratio increases (excluding overload-protected) OR control plane timeouts increase.
- For shed_rate alerts:
  - WARN if overload_protected_error_ratio > 2% for 15m (customer awareness)
  - PAGE if overload_protected_error_ratio > 10% for 30m AND affects paid tiers (tier!=free)
  - Add per-tier thresholds (free can tolerate higher shed without paging; paid tiers page earlier)

C) Queue depth / latency
- Adjust windows:
  - queue_depth: use 10m rolling + require p99 latency degradation in same period
  - p99 latency: evaluate over 10m, not 2m, for paging
- Add “runaway queue” hard page:
  - PAGE if queue_depth > hard_cap*0.9 for 5m AND shed_rate is NOT increasing (indicates breaker not engaging / bug)

D) Notification hygiene
- Grouping: group alerts by (region, model_family, tier) rather than per model revision to reduce duplication.
- Add cooldown on notification routing: if same alert fires repeatedly within 30m, suppress duplicates and update existing incident annotation.

Implementation plan
1) Pull canary metrics
- Use the canary time window and export alert firing history (Grafana + Alertmanager) for: breaker_open, breaker_transitions, shed_rate, queue_depth, p99 latency, internal 5xx.
- Output: a short table of “alerts fired -> was it actionable?” with suggested threshold/window adjustments.

2) Draft updated alert rules
- Update alert definitions in observability-pack repo (same location as pr-611).
- Update runbook links in annotations to point to the Hosted overload mitigation runbook section “Alert interpretation (post-canary)”.

3) Review
- SRE review: Rafael Mendes, Christine Wong
- Observability review: Allison Grant (cardinality + sampling considerations)
- Oncall review: Tomáš Novák (paging policy alignment)

4) Rollout
- Apply changes first to canary region/model set for 48h.
- Validate:
  - pages/week decreases
  - no missed detection in synthetic overload drill (game-day scenario replay)

Acceptance criteria
- Reduce alert pages attributed to overload-protection alert set by >= 60% compared to canary baseline week, without increasing mean time to detect genuine regressions.
- No more than 1 page per overload event for the same underlying condition (dedupe working).
- Clear split in paging logic: internal failures page; expected load shedding mostly warns/annotates.

Open questions
- What is the correct paid-tier paging threshold for sustained overload_protected_error_ratio? (Need PM input from Nikhil Sharma / Henry Cho.)
- Do we need separate thresholds per model class (long-context vs standard) due to different recovery times?

Links
- ENG-4830 (Dashboards)
- ENG-4829 (Metrics + traces)
- ENG-4834 (Canary rollout)
- observability-pack/pr-611 (initial dashboard + alert rules)
- slo-toolkit/pr-204 (SLO accounting: overload-protected errors)

Updates / comments
2026-01-22 (Sergio Costa)
- Pulled first 48h of canary alert history. 9 pages; 6 were non-actionable duplicates during recovery. Primary offenders: breaker transition count + short-window shed_rate.
- Action: switching breaker paging to sustained-open as proposed above.

2026-01-28 (Christine Wong)
- +1 to flapping detector as WARN-only. Paging on transition count caused confusion (“system is protecting itself but we page anyway”).
- Note: include hysteresis cooldown changes from the hotfix (pr-18519) in runbook context so people don’t misdiagnose.

2026-02-03 (Allison Grant)
- Please avoid labels with unbounded model_version; group by model_family and tier. Keep region label.
- For flapping detector, compute from breaker state transitions metric with sampling; don’t emit per-request.

2026-02-06 (Sergio Costa)
- Drafted new rules and grouping in a branch (will open PR early next week). Also adding alert annotations: “This is expected during controlled overload. Page only if internal 5xx elevated.”
- Pending: PM sign-off on paid-tier thresholds + exact wording for oncall annotations.
